title: The Gysin class of a local complete intersection morphism is independent of the chosen factorization
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y a local complete intersection morphism of schemes locally of finite type over (S, delta), the lemma asserts that the bivariant class f^! is independent of the choice of a factorization f = g o i with g smooth, provided such a factorization exists (statement lines 13484-13492). The proof reduces an arbitrary second factorization to a comparison diagram: given f = g' o i' as well one first passes to the smooth morphism g'' : P x_Y P' -> Y and the immersion i'' : X -> P x_Y P', so that it suffices to treat a diagram X -> P -> Y and X -> P' -> Y with p : P' -> P smooth, and then, because (g')^* = p^* o g^* by Lemma labelled lemma-compose-flat-pullback, to show that i^! = (i')^! o p^* in A^*(X -> P) (proof lines 13494-13509). The proof considers the cartesian diagram with X x_P P' and the section s = (1, i'), notes that s and j are regular immersions by Divisors, Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-section-smooth-regular-immersion and Lemma labelled divisors-lemma-flat-base-change-regular-immersion, and that i' = j o s, so that (i')^! = s^! o j^! by Lemma labelled lemma-composition-regular-immersion (proof lines 13511-13519). Since the square is cartesian, j^! is the restriction of i^! to P' by Lemma labelled lemma-construction-gysin, and because bivariant classes commute with flat pullbacks one has j^! o p^* = p-bar^* o i^!, so it remains to show s^! o p-bar^* = id, which is Lemma labelled lemma-section-smooth (proof lines 13521-13527). Reducing an arbitrary pair of factorizations to a single smooth comparison via the fibre product and then splitting the immersion through a section is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
